clue.text: Commanders following soldiers in retreat, overwrought?

indicators.note: the commanders come after the soldiers, so their letters are placed second
troops in retreat go backwards, so the word for soldiers is read from right to left

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers
CO, commanding officer, twice for the plural

explanation.surface: Officers trailing behind fleeing troops are in an overwrought state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' marks a reversal of the soldiers' letters only. The question mark flags a pun: overwrought here means elaborately ornamented, not agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: The rococo style is famous for its excessively ornate, fussy decoration, so it is overworked in the decorative sense.

clue.text: Despised person coming up with term that's unpleasant

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a leper is a social outcast, someone shunned
Lent is the spring term at some universities and law courts

explanation.surface: An outcast arrives with a phrase that is offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' is a reversal in a down clue. Lent is the name of a spring university or legal term, not only the season before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent drives people away because it is disgusting or distasteful.

clue.text: Pine, say, as prisoner, long-term one being executed

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: an execution here is a beheading, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence

explanation.surface: An inmate pines away, as does a fellow life-sentence prisoner facing execution.
explanation.walkthrough: Pine looks like a verb about longing, but it is the tree. 'being executed' beheads LIFER to IFER.
explanation.definitionFit: The pine is a cone-bearing evergreen tree, so it is an example of that group, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Take stock

explanation.walkthrough: Take stock reads as one phrase meaning review; split it into two senses of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry something is to take it with you, and a shop that carries a line keeps it in stock.

clue.text: Endless supply of grouse, rabbit, and bird

indicators.note: with no end, the word for grouse loses its final letter

parts.note: to grouse is to complain, to whine
to rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering, to chat

explanation.surface: A game larder holds plenty of grouse, rabbit and another bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the E from WHINE. Grouse and rabbit look like game for the pot, but both are verbs here: complain and talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The whinchat is a small brown songbird of heaths and grassland.

clue.text: Do this to avoid danger of sticking in needle game

definitions.text: Do this to avoid danger of sticking in needle game

parts.words: Do this to avoid danger of sticking in needle game
parts.note: a sewer protects a fingertip with a metal cap so the needle does not prick; if you cannot find it, go searching, and the search is a children's parlour game

explanation.surface: Advice for a sewer worried about pricking a finger during a needlework session.
explanation.walkthrough: The parlour game in which a small object is hidden in a room for the others to find is named after the sewing cap that guards the finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional children's party game where players search the room for a hidden small sewing object.

clue.text: Flower child regarding himself as one of the beautiful people

definitions.text: child regarding himself as one of the beautiful people

explanation.surface: A flower child of the sixties considers himself one of the beautiful people.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower child suggests a hippy; split it. In Greek myth a beautiful youth, son of a river god, fell in love with his own reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil genus bears this name, as did the youth of myth who gazed at his own reflection in a pool.

clue.text: Superior degree course in more than one respect

explanation.surface: A top university course is admirable in several ways.
explanation.walkthrough: A British honours degree is a bachelor's course of higher standard than an ordinary pass degree.
explanation.definitionFit: An honours degree is the higher bachelor's programme, and honour also means esteem, so the plural means several marks of esteem.

clue.text: As shown by Goethe, Mephistopheles' recurrent idea

indicators.note: the letters are shown, on display, inside the writer's and character's names run together

explanation.surface: Goethe's Faust illustrates the devil Mephistopheles' obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: Mephistopheles is the devil in Goethe's Faust, which makes the literary surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject or motif running through a work of art or music is its central repeated idea.

clue.text: Go off the rails with lousy Italian or Spanish ecclesiastic

indicators.note: going off the rails is going wildly astray, so the letters around it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A churchman, whether a seedy Italian or a Spaniard, goes astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the rails' shuffles GO with LOUSY ITALIAN. Go reads as part of the phrase go off the rails, but it is also fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Basque priest who founded the Jesuit order in the sixteenth century was a Spanish churchman later made a saint.

clue.text: Shut up intimidating woman, former British leader

parts.note: to pen an animal is to shut it up in an enclosure
a dragon is a fierce, formidable woman

explanation.surface: Someone tells a formidable woman to be quiet, and she turns out to be an ex-prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a modern politician, but the leader is the legendary Uther Pendragon, chief of the ancient Britons and father of King Arthur.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendragon was the title of a supreme chief among the ancient Britons, borne by Uther, King Arthur's father.

clue.text: New addition to fashion collection

indicators.note: the letter for new is added into the middle of the word for fashion

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion, as in all the rage

explanation.surface: A designer has added a new item to this season's fashion line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'addition to' puts N inside RAGE. The surface's fashion collection is a decoy: the definition is collection on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a set or line of products offered together, such as a range of garden furniture.

clue.text: Trot, perhaps, a short distance into field

indicators.note: the distance abbreviation is put into the word for a field

parts.note: a ley is a piece of grassland or meadow
FT, a foot, abbreviated, so doubly short

explanation.surface: A horse trots a little way into a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: Trot looks like a horse's pace, but with its capital it is short for Trotskyist, an example of a left-winger, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trotskyist is a far left-winger, and a lefty is an informal name for any left-winger.

clue.text: A tax on West End property

indicators.note: in an across clue the tax is put on, that is after, the letter from West
the end of the word West is its final letter

parts.note: a tribute is a payment exacted by a ruler, a form of tax

explanation.surface: A levy is imposed on real estate in London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: West End reads as the London district, but 'End' picks the T from West. A and T are followed by TRIBUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a quality or characteristic belonging to someone, a property in the philosophical sense.

clue.text: Listener has abandoned materialism

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who once listened to spiritual teaching has given up on worldly values.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges the eleven letters of LISTENER HAS. The obvious start, EAR for listener, is a trap that leaves the rest unaccounted for.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worldly and concerned with physical things rather than spiritual ones is the core of a materialistic outlook.

clue.text: Overworked pair of journalists repressing urge to move North

indicators.note: to repress is to hold down or contain, so the reversed urge goes inside the journalists

parts.note: a hack and an ED, editor, two newspaper people

indicators.note: in a down clue moving north means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing or urge

explanation.surface: Two exhausted reporters are suppressing a desire to relocate up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move North' reverses the urge in a down clue, and 'repressing' holds it inside the two journalists. Hack is slang for a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase used so often it has lost its force is described as worn out, stale and trite.

clue.text: Dominant, like this Labour leader

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of the Labour Party is described as dominant.
explanation.walkthrough: Dominant reads as a description of the party leader, but it is the musical term: in tonic sol-fa, soh or sol is the fifth note of the scale, the dominant.
explanation.definitionFit: In sol-fa singing names the fifth degree of the scale, called the dominant, is sung as soh, also written sol.

clue.text: No professional players represented cricket side

indicators.note: represented is read as re-presented, presented again in a new order

parts.note: the on side, or leg side, is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Amateur players were picked to play for a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges PLAYERS to LAYPERS. In cricket the field is divided into the off side and the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without expert training or membership of a profession is a non-specialist.

clue.text: Crack — drug that must be rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for the drug is read backwards

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Crack cocaine is a drug that ought to be turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack looks like the drug, but it is the adjective meaning first-rate, as in crack troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Crack, as in a crack shot, means excellent, of the highest quality, just as top does.

clue.text: Trip over, say, like a fool

annotationWithheld.why: Trip over, say, like a fool (7): no parse found for the wordplay part 'over, say, like a fool' giving the letters for PASSAGE beyond the ASS for fool
annotationWithheld.clue: Trip over, say, like a fool

clue.text: An invalid account, perhaps

parts.note: read invalid not as null and void but as a sick person: the record of a patient's illness kept by doctors

explanation.surface: A bookkeeping account has been declared void.
explanation.walkthrough: Invalid with the stress on the first syllable is a sick person, and their account is the medical record of their condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's file tracing a patient's illness and treatment over time is the record kept for an ailing person.

clue.text: The sin of hoarding

parts.note: a hoarding is a temporary board fence round a building site

explanation.surface: Greed in storing things up is a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoarding looks like greedy stockpiling but is the British word for a board fence or billboard. The opening 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoing or transgression against a moral or legal code is what the sin is.

clue.text: Deceive female teacher, say, during class

indicators.note: say signals a word as it is spoken, so the title is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: pupils address a woman teacher as Miss
in means during, as in in the summer
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A schoolmistress tells untruths in front of her pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives MIS, sounding like MISS; then IN for during and FORM for class. School forms are British year groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone false information is to mislead or deceive them.

clue.text: Doctor qualified to raise subject that often recurs

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a military doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it, so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: fit means qualified or suitable

explanation.surface: A physician is competent to bring up a topic that keeps returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' is a reversal in a down clue. MO, medical officer, is the usual crossword doctor alongside DR and GP.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring element or image in a work of art or music is its distinctive repeated feature.

clue.text: So-called coarse fish

indicators.note: so-called means named or spoken of this way, pointing to how the word is pronounced

parts.note: rough means coarse, as in rough cloth

explanation.surface: An angler names a type of coarse fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Coarse fish is an angling term for freshwater fish other than salmon and trout, which tempts you to read the clue as one phrase; coarse is the sound piece and fish the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruffe is a small freshwater perch found in British rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Get a rocket, perhaps, for seeking inspiration from the past

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a firework to look for inspiration in history.
explanation.walkthrough: A retro is short for a retrorocket, fired to slow a spacecraft; 'Get a' and 'for' only join the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A retro-rocket is a braking engine on a spacecraft, and nostalgic styling imitates fashions of earlier decades.

clue.text: Play in which a Duke's an awful flatterer

indicators.note: in which shows the following letters going inside the word for play

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

explanation.surface: In a stage play, a duke turns out to be a dreadful sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts A and D inside TOY. Play looks like a drama but is the verb toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a fawning sycophant who flatters people of influence, a contemptible type.

clue.text: Sharpeners for tools — special ones I lost

indicators.note: special suggests something made differently, prompting a new arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A craftsman laments losing some particular whetstones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges ONES I LOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine-grained stones lubricated with oil are used for honing blades and chisels.

clue.text: Like a shrink, runs into quarrel with fellow

indicators.note: the runs letter goes into the word for a quarrel

parts.note: a feud is a long-running quarrel
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
Ian is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: Someone acting like a psychiatrist gets into an argument with a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrink is slang for a psychiatrist; Freud founded psychoanalysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychoanalytic in manner, in the tradition of Sigmund Freud, the founding figure of the psychiatric profession's talking cure.

clue.text: As players, appear to improve

explanation.surface: Performers take the stage in order to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: Players come on when they walk onto a stage or pitch; a pupil who comes on makes progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors or substitutes enter the scene, and separately the phrase means to progress or get better.
